title: Trump’s Oil Deal Needs the Houthis to Behave
author: John Authers, Richard Abbey
summary: John Authers 指出，胡塞武装袭击沙特机场与能源设施，推动布伦特原油回到每桶 106 美元，半年远期价格创纪录，市场已放弃冲突很快结束的预期。美俄放松柴油出口制裁的协议被解读为美国急于压低油价，柴油价格仍接近历史高位。关键变量是沙特如何报复，以及胡塞是否威胁红海航运和延布出口设施；此外金价依然坚挺。

paragraphs.text: To get John Authers’ newsletter delivered directly to your inbox, sign up here .
Today’s Points:
In Ukraine, strikes on energy facilities look set to continue.
Saudi Arabia is still fending off attacks on its own oil facilities.
Chips sold off on a quiet Columbus Day ahead of earnings.
Despite everything, the gold price is proving resilient.
AND: Buon compleannno to Luciano Pavarotti.
Troubled Waters for Oil

The Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia’s airports are only the latest catalyst driving oil prices higher. Brent crude first-month futures are back to $106 per barrel, while the price for six months hence has reached a record as investors abandon the notion that this conflict will be over soon:
Oil is still swayed by geopolitical moves, and near its highest in a month as Riyadh weighs an appropriate response to the deadly attacks:

All of this is despite last week’s controversial deal with Russia to lift sanctions on diesel exports, and President Donald Trump’s appeals for Ukraine to desist from striking Russian energy infrastructure. Far from taking confidence, markets seem to be interpreting this as US desperation. Diesel is close to its all-time high, and moved little after the deal:
Tina Fordham of Fordham Global Foresight argues that investors could be underestimating the risks to energy prices and supply security, and called a turning point in US-Russian relations:

Any escalation elsewhere that erodes Trump’s efforts to cushion prices at the pump won’t be taken lightly. The question now is less whether Saudi Arabia retaliates so much as how far it might be prepared to roil an already strained energy market even further.
The US will be reluctant to deploy forces to assist the Saudis, but it’s hard to predict how this front will unfold. Bloomberg Intelligence’s Dina Esfandiary says it is not a zero-sum game:

So far, Houthi attacks on energy infrastructure have been relatively contained. This, BCA Research’s Marko Papic argues, may reflect a deliberate effort by the Houthis to avoid sending oil prices surging and thus putting themselves in Washington’s crosshairs:

They are no match for the might of the US. But the problems that America has had dealing with Iran in the Strait of Hormuz, despite obvious military superiority, show that isn’t the point. Pushed into a corner, the Houthis’ ability to inflict damage on energy facilities or disrupt oil shipments through the Red Sea, the other key Middle East shipping route, cannot be dismissed.

One notable example is the East-West pipeline network and export complex in the industrial city of Yanbu. Weeks ago, an attack from an Iraqi militia was effectively contained. Still, Capital Economics’ Jason Tuvey points out that there’s no guarantee another attack, this time from the Houthis, wouldn’t cause more lasting disruption. The pipeline can handle 7 million barrels a day, but limited capacity at Yanbu capped shipments of crude and refined products at 3.5 million to 4 million barrels per day from April to July, as this Capital Economics chart shows:

Any response that pushes the Houthis to broaden their attacks would be detrimental to oil prices. Unlike at the onset of the Iran war, oil prices are already elevated, and escalation aggravates the pain. A shutdown of routes that bypass Hormuz could easily bring the price past $120.
A Bullion Resistance

Gold is showing remarkable resilience despite one of its poorest runs in the past five years. The cocktail of factors weighing on it is led by the Federal Reserve’s return to rate hikes, which has driven the dollar to multi-month highs, and heightened inflation expectations caused by the Middle East war. Real 10-year yields, long regarded as having a key inverse relationship with the gold price as it pays no income, have risen a full percentage point this year to 2.88%. And yet while gold is down, it has only dropped about 3% during the same time:

This is damaging because gold has been seen as a hedge against debasement, or a fecklessly loose US monetary policy. Such fears drove its rally to record highs back in January. Since then, the Fed under Kevin Warsh has proven more hawkish than expected, and gold’s return as of last Friday is among the weakest in the last decade, behind only 2022, another year marked by a surprising return to rate hikes. This slide could have been a lot worse but for structural demand largely driven by central banks, which has somewhat put a floor under gold:

The World Gold Council’s most recent data on reserve accumulation show that the metal still appeals to monetary authorities, led by China, despite expectations of higher US interest rates. Does this demand have staying power? The council’s survey shows that 45% of policymakers plan to increase their holdings over the next year – mostly leaning on gold’s ability to hedge geopolitical risks as well as a long-term store of value:

Constraints on mine production have kept supply from keeping pace with demand. Output increased only 2% year-on-year in the second quarter. As Stonegate’s David Storms points out, new mines require years of exploration, permitting, financing and construction, while mature operations face grade decline and rising capital requirements. The bullish argument is that gold prices could re-rate well before the industry brings meaningful new production online.

Another support for gold is the continuous flow of money into gold-backed exchange-traded funds. September net inflows surged more than in any month since the first quarter of 2022, according to Bloomberg:

Over the past two weeks, bullion has shrugged off structural headwinds and recouped about 2% of its losses. Whether the rebound holds will depend in part on September’s inflation data, due Wednesday. Record fuel prices could keep the latest reading elevated, with the both the headline (from 3.4% to 3.6%) and the core (from 2.4% to 2.5%) rates of CPI expected to tick upward. That might increase the pressure on bullion by raising the prospect of interest rates staying higher for longer. Against that, if the Trump administration’s deal with Russia to release more diesel works out — despite the many levels of political disagreement surrounding it — traders may be less bothered by backward-looking inflation numbers.

Beyond this immediate catalyst, TD Securities’ Ryan McKay argues that geopolitical risks, fiscal concerns, dollar debasement, de-dollarization and stagflation fears remain firmly in play. That would allow gold to decouple from real interest rates and embark on a new bull run into 2027. Louis-Vincent Gave of Gavekal Research holds a similar favorable outlook:

The big spike in yields even as gold’s price remains relatively contained underscores the extent of bullion’s resistance. While it’s premature to suggest a new norm, it’s striking how gold prices have held up in the face of surging yields:

A favorable outlook would feed into gold equities. Daniel Major of UBS projects that gold prices above $4,000 an ounce would help margins, making free cash flows attractive. But he he still urges caution, looking to avoid negative cost guidance or production downgrades and mergers and acquisitions’ risk:

Complications in the bull case for gold remain. If rates stay higher for longer, it will have to contend with a stronger dollar and higher costs of holding an asset that pays no income. Those forces could blunt any rally, even as central-bank buying and geopolitical uncertainty continue to lend support.
Survival Tips

A happy birthday to Luciano Pavarotti. The great tenor, who passed away in 2007, would have turned 92 today. Like many performers, he was a complicated human being. Back in 1993, I was lucky enough to sing in his backing choir when he was at the peak of his popularity and performing before crowds of 20,000 — and soon discovered why musicians didn’t like working with him. Downright rude much of the time and unapologetic that he didn’t feel equal to singing Nessun Dorma, the Puccini aria that had become his signature when his recording of it was used as the theme song for the 1990 World Cup. This didn’t make him any less of an artist, but it was difficult to accept that he seemed to have taken his God-given talent as a license to disrespect colleagues. Are there any other nominations for people who might have done the same thing?
And for why people let him get away with it, try lapping up his genius in this, this, this, this (with Sheryl Crow) and this.

annotations.meaningZh: 直接投递到你的收件箱
annotations.lemma: deliver something directly to someone's inbox
annotations.explanation: 新闻邮件订阅常见表达，deliver 在这里是“投递、发送”的意思，不是“递送货物”。

examples.en: The report will be delivered directly to your inbox every morning.

annotations.explanation: strike 在此为名词“袭击、打击”，介词用 on；energy facilities 指发电站、油气管网等能源基础设施。

examples.en: The strikes on power plants worsened the blackout.
examples.zh: 对发电厂的袭击加剧了停电。

annotations.meaningZh: 看来将会继续；势将继续

examples.en: Prices look set to rise again next month.
examples.zh: 下个月价格看来还将再次上涨。

annotations.explanation: fend off 常与 attacks、questions、criticism 等搭配，表示挡开、抵御。

examples.en: The company is trying to fend off a hostile takeover.
examples.zh: 该公司正试图抵御一场敌意收购。

annotations.explanation: 这里不是“薯条”，而是市场报道中对半导体芯片公司股票的简称。

examples.en: Chips led the market lower on Friday.
examples.zh: 周五芯片股领跌大盘。

annotations.explanation: 金融语境中 sell off 表示投资者大量卖出某类资产，导致价格下跌。

examples.en: Technology stocks sold off after the rate decision.
examples.zh: 利率决议后科技股遭到抛售。

annotations.explanation: ahead of 表示“在……之前”；earnings 指公司财报、盈利报告。

examples.en: The shares were volatile ahead of earnings.
examples.zh: 财报公布前股价波动较大。

annotations.meaningZh: 哥伦布日（美国联邦假日，市场交投通常清淡）

examples.en: Bond markets were closed for Columbus Day.
examples.zh: 债市因哥伦布日休市。

annotations.explanation: 用于让步，表示尽管有种种不利或复杂情况。

examples.en: Despite everything, she remains optimistic.
examples.zh: 尽管如此，她仍然乐观。

annotations.explanation: prove 后可接形容词，表示“证明是、表现出”；resilient 常形容价格、经济等抗压。

examples.en: Demand has proved resilient despite higher prices.
examples.zh: 尽管价格上涨，需求仍表现出韧性。

annotations.meaningZh: 生日快乐（意大利语；原文拼写多了一个 n）
annotations.explanation: 意大利语生日祝福。原文 compleannno 拼写多了一个 n，学习时注意正确形式是 compleanno。

examples.en: Buon compleanno!
examples.zh: 生日快乐！

annotations.meaningZh: 卢奇亚诺·帕瓦罗蒂，意大利男高音歌唱家
annotations.explanation: 世界三大男高音之一，此处作为文化人物出现。

examples.en: Pavarotti was celebrated for his powerful tenor voice.
examples.zh: 帕瓦罗蒂以其强有力的男高音闻名。

annotations.explanation: 字面为“汹涌的水域”，常比喻困难、动荡或危险局面；标题中指石油市场面临麻烦。

examples.en: The economy is entering troubled waters.
examples.zh: 经济正进入动荡水域。

annotations.meaningZh: 胡塞武装（也门反政府武装组织）
annotations.explanation: 也门胡塞运动及其武装力量，常出现在中东地缘政治报道中。

examples.en: The Houthis claimed responsibility for the attack.
examples.zh: 胡塞武装宣称对袭击负责。

target.text: the latest catalyst driving oil prices higher

annotations.meaningZh: 推高油价的最新催化因素
annotations.explanation: catalyst 本为化学“催化剂”，商业新闻中常指推动价格或事件变化的因素。

examples.en: The outage was the latest catalyst driving copper prices higher.
examples.zh: 这次停产是推高铜价的最新催化因素。

annotations.explanation: Brent crude 是国际油价基准；first-month futures 指最近交割月份的期货合约。

examples.en: Brent crude first-month futures jumped after the news.
examples.zh: 消息公布后布伦特原油近月期货跳涨。

annotations.explanation: hence 表示“从此以后”，months hence 是较正式或书面化的“数月之后”。

examples.en: The contract expires two years hence.
examples.zh: 该合同两年后到期。

annotations.explanation: record 在此为名词，表示历史最高或最低纪录；常搭配 reach、hit、set。

examples.en: The index reached a record last week.
examples.zh: 该指数上周创下纪录。

annotations.explanation: notion 是“观念、想法”，abandon the notion that 表示不再相信某个判断。

examples.en: Investors have abandoned the notion that rates will fall soon.
examples.zh: 投资者已不再认为利率会很快下降。

annotations.explanation: sway 本义“摇摆”，引申为“影响、左右”；be swayed by 强调被外部因素影响。

examples.en: The market was swayed by political headlines.
examples.zh: 市场受到政治新闻的影响。

annotations.meaningZh: 地缘政治动向；地缘政治举措
annotations.explanation: move 在此指行动、举措；geopolitical moves 常指国家间的战略动作。

examples.en: Oil traders are watching geopolitical moves closely.
examples.zh: 石油交易员正密切关注地缘政治动向。

target.text: near its highest in a month

annotations.lemma: near one's highest in a month
annotations.explanation: 用于描述价格接近一段时间以来的最高水平。

examples.en: The euro is near its highest in three months.
examples.zh: 欧元接近三个月高位。

annotations.meaningZh: 利雅得；此处借指沙特阿拉伯政府
annotations.explanation: 新闻中常用首都名指代该国政府，类似 Washington 指美国政府。

examples.en: Riyadh has not yet commented on the attack.
examples.zh: 沙特政府尚未对袭击置评。

annotations.explanation: weigh 在此不是“称重”，而是“权衡、考虑”；常用 weigh options、weigh a response。

examples.en: The government is weighing its response to the tariff.
examples.zh: 政府正在权衡对关税的回应。

annotations.explanation: lift 常与 sanctions、ban、restriction 搭配，表示取消、解除。

examples.en: The deal would lift sanctions on several sectors.
examples.zh: 该协议将解除对几个行业的制裁。

target.text: appeals for Ukraine to desist from striking

annotations.lemma: appeal for someone to desist from doing something
annotations.explanation: desist from 是正式用语，表示“停止做某事”；appeal for someone to do 表示呼吁某人做某事。

examples.en: The UN appealed for both sides to desist from attacking civilians.
examples.zh: 联合国呼吁双方停止袭击平民。

annotations.explanation: far from 表示“远非、非但不”，常用来形成反差：不但没有 A，反而 B。

examples.en: Far from calming investors, the statement increased anxiety.
examples.zh: 该声明非但没有安抚投资者，反而加剧了焦虑。

annotations.explanation: interpret A as B 表示“把 A 理解为/解读为 B”。

examples.en: Markets interpreted the move as a sign of weakness.
examples.zh: 市场将此举措解读为疲软迹象。

annotations.explanation: all-time 表示“空前的、历史最高的”，常与 high、low、record 连用。

examples.en: Gold hit an all-time high earlier this year.
examples.zh: 黄金今年早些时候创下历史新高。

annotations.explanation: 市场报道中 move 指价格变动；moved little 表示几乎没怎么动。

examples.en: The stock moved little after the announcement.
examples.zh: 公告后该股变动不大。

annotations.explanation: risk to something 表示对某事物的风险；underestimate 是“低估”。

examples.en: Investors may be underestimating the risks to supply.
examples.zh: 投资者可能低估了供应面临的风险。

annotations.explanation: 能源、粮食等领域常用术语，指供应不受中断威胁的状态。

examples.en: The war has raised concerns about energy supply security.
examples.zh: 战争引发了对能源供应安全的担忧。

annotations.explanation: 通常搭配是 call something a turning point；原文中 call 后直接接 a turning point，可理解为“称之为一个转折点”。

examples.en: Analysts called the deal a turning point in the conflict.
examples.zh: 分析人士称该协议是冲突的转折点。

annotations.explanation: 指冲突、紧张局势等加剧；新闻中常与 conflict、war、tensions 搭配。

examples.en: Any escalation could push prices higher.
examples.zh: 任何升级都可能推高价格。

annotations.explanation: erode 本义“侵蚀”，引申为逐步削弱、损害。

examples.en: Inflation is eroding household purchasing power.
examples.zh: 通胀正在侵蚀家庭购买力。

annotations.meaningZh: 缓冲加油泵价格；抑制零售油价
annotations.explanation: at the pump 指在加油站加油时；cushion prices 表示减轻价格上涨的冲击。

examples.en: The tax cut is meant to cushion prices at the pump.
examples.zh: 减税旨在缓冲加油价格。

annotations.meaningZh: 不会被等闲视之；不会被轻视
annotations.explanation: take something lightly 表示轻视、不认真对待；被动式 won’t be taken lightly 表示不会被忽视。

examples.en: Such threats should not be taken lightly.
examples.zh: 此类威胁不应被轻视。

annotations.meaningZh: 与其说……不如说……（与 less 搭配）
annotations.explanation: less A so much as B 表示“与其说是 A，不如说是 B”，用于强调真正的问题在 B。

examples.en: It is less a crisis so much as a warning.
examples.zh: 这与其说是一场危机，不如说是一个警告。

annotations.explanation: roil 常指搅浑液体，也常比喻扰乱市场、局势，语体较正式。

examples.en: The scandal roiled financial markets.
examples.zh: 这起丑闻搅动了金融市场。

annotations.meaningZh: 已经紧张不安的能源市场
annotations.explanation: strained 表示紧张、承压的；strained market 指供应或情绪已很紧张的市场。

examples.en: The news added pressure to an already strained market.
examples.zh: 这一消息给本已紧张的市场增加了压力。

target.text: The question now is less whether Saudi Arabia retaliates so much as how far it might be prepared to roil an already strained energy market even further.

annotations.translationZh: 现在的问题与其说是沙特阿拉伯是否会报复，不如说是它可能准备把本已紧张的能源市场进一步搅乱到什么程度。
annotations.explanation: less ... so much as ... 是常见比较结构，表示“与其说……不如说……”。这里连接两个 wh- 从句，突出问题的重点已经从“是否报复”转向“报复到什么程度”。

structure.note: “沙特是否报复”是较次要的一面

structure.text: so much as how far it might be prepared to roil an already strained energy market even further
structure.note: 真正强调的是“可能把市场搅乱到何种程度”

examples.en: The issue is less whether they will act so much as how far they will go.
examples.zh: 问题与其说是他们是否会行动，不如说是他们会做到什么程度。

annotations.explanation: reluctant to do 表示不愿做；deploy forces 是军事术语“部署部队”。

examples.en: The government is reluctant to deploy troops abroad.
examples.zh: 政府不愿向海外部署军队。

annotations.explanation: 可指事件、局面逐渐展开或发展，新闻中常用 how events unfold。

examples.en: It is hard to predict how the situation will unfold.
examples.zh: 很难预测局势将如何发展。

annotations.explanation: 指一方所得必为另一方所失的局面；常用于国际关系、商业竞争。

examples.en: Trade is not always a zero-sum game.
examples.zh: 贸易并不总是零和博弈。

annotations.explanation: contained 在此表示“受控制的、未扩大的”，不是“包含的”。

examples.en: The damage was relatively contained.
examples.zh: 损害相对受控。

annotations.explanation: deliberate 表示有意为之、故意的，强调不是偶然。

examples.en: It was a deliberate effort to mislead the public.
examples.zh: 这是故意误导公众的行为。

annotations.explanation: send something surging 表示使某物急剧上涨；surging 作宾语补足语。

examples.en: The news sent shares surging.
examples.zh: 这一消息使股价飙升。

annotations.meaningZh: 使自己成为华盛顿的打击目标
annotations.explanation: crosshairs 是瞄准镜中的十字准星；in someone’s crosshairs 比喻成为某人的目标。Washington 借指美国政府。

examples.en: The company put itself in regulators’ crosshairs.
examples.zh: 该公司把自己变成了监管机构的目标。

annotations.explanation: match 在此指“对手、匹敌者”；be no match for 表示实力悬殊，不是对手。

examples.en: The small force was no match for the invading army.
examples.zh: 这支小部队不是入侵军队的对手。

annotations.explanation: 此处不是情态动词“可能”，而是名词“力量、威力”，常见于 military might、economic might。

examples.en: The country’s economic might is declining.
examples.zh: 该国的经济实力正在下降。

annotations.explanation: 全球最重要的石油运输咽喉之一，连接波斯湾和阿拉伯海。

examples.en: A closure of the Strait of Hormuz would shock oil markets.
examples.zh: 霍尔木兹海峡若被封锁将冲击石油市场。

annotations.meaningZh: 关键不在这里；这不是重点
annotations.explanation: 用于反驳论证重点，表示某个事实虽真实但不改变核心问题。

examples.en: Yes, they are weaker, but that isn’t the point.
examples.zh: 是的，他们更弱，但这不是重点。

annotations.explanation: 比喻被逼到没有退路，只能反击或采取极端行动。

examples.en: Pushed into a corner, the firm had to sell assets.
examples.zh: 被逼到绝境，该公司不得不出售资产。

annotations.explanation: inflict 常与 damage、pain、harm 搭配，表示造成伤害或损害。

examples.en: The storm inflicted severe damage on coastal towns.
examples.zh: 风暴对沿海城镇造成严重破坏。

annotations.meaningZh: 不能被忽视；不能被小觑
annotations.explanation: dismiss 在此表示“不予考虑、轻视”；cannot be dismissed 强调不可忽略。

examples.en: The risk of further attacks cannot be dismissed.
examples.zh: 进一步袭击的风险不能被忽视。

target.text: Pushed into a corner, the Houthis’ ability to inflict damage on energy facilities or disrupt oil shipments through the Red Sea, the other key Middle East shipping route, cannot be dismissed.

annotations.translationZh: 若被逼到角落，胡塞武装对能源设施造成破坏、或扰乱经红海这条中东另一关键航运路线的石油运输的能力，不能被小觑。
annotations.explanation: 句首 Pushed into a corner 是过去分词短语作状语，表示条件或原因；主语中心词是 ability，后面接不定式短语，中间插入同位语解释 Red Sea。谓语是 cannot be dismissed。

structure.note: 表示“若被逼到角落/走投无路时”

structure.text: to inflict damage on energy facilities or disrupt oil shipments through the Red Sea
structure.role: 不定式短语作后置定语
structure.note: 说明 ability 的具体内容

structure.text: the other key Middle East shipping route
structure.note: 解释 Red Sea 是中东另一关键航运路线
被动结构，表示不能被忽视

examples.en: Pushed into a corner, the small country’s ability to disrupt trade cannot be dismissed.
examples.zh: 若被逼到角落，这个小国扰乱贸易的能力不能被小觑。

annotations.meaningZh: 显著例子；值得注意的例子
annotations.explanation: notable 表示值得注意的、显著的，比 example 更有强调意味。

examples.en: A notable example is the 1970s oil shock.
examples.zh: 一个显著例子是1970年代的石油危机。

annotations.explanation: 此处不是形容词“复杂的”，而是名词“综合设施、建筑群”，如 export complex。

examples.en: The port and industrial complex employs thousands.
examples.zh: 这个港口和工业综合设施雇用了数千人。

annotations.explanation: 用于表示某事没有把握，后面常接 that 从句。

examples.en: There’s no guarantee that prices will fall.
examples.zh: 不能保证价格会下跌。

annotations.explanation: lasting 表示持续的、持久的；disruption 指中断、扰乱。

examples.en: The strike caused lasting disruption to supply chains.
examples.zh: 罢工对供应链造成了持久扰乱。

target.text: capped shipments of crude and refined products at

annotations.meaningZh: 将原油和成品油运输量限制在……
annotations.explanation: cap 作动词表示“给……设上限”；shipments 指运输量、出货量。

examples.en: The group capped output at 5 million barrels a day.
examples.zh: 该组织将产量限制在每天500万桶。

annotations.explanation: 能源行业术语；crude 指原油，refined products 指汽油、柴油等精炼产品。

examples.en: The ban covers crude and refined products.
examples.zh: 该禁令涵盖原油和成品油。

target.text: as this Capital Economics chart shows

annotations.meaningZh: 如资本经济公司这张图表所示
annotations.explanation: as ... shows 是引证图表、数据时的常用表达。

examples.en: As this chart shows, demand has slowed.
examples.zh: 如这张图表所示，需求已经放缓。

annotations.explanation: detrimental 是正式用词，常搭配 to，表示造成损害。

examples.en: Higher tariffs are detrimental to consumers.
examples.zh: 更高关税对消费者不利。

annotations.explanation: onset 表示开始、爆发，常用于战争、疾病、危机等。

examples.en: Prices rose sharply at the onset of the war.
examples.zh: 战争开始时价格大幅上涨。

annotations.explanation: 形容价格、水平等高于正常或此前水平，不是“被举起的”。

examples.en: Oil prices remain elevated.
examples.zh: 油价仍然高企。

annotations.explanation: aggravate 表示使恶化、加剧，常与 pain、problem、crisis 搭配。

examples.en: The delay only aggravates the pain for consumers.
examples.zh: 拖延只会加剧消费者的痛苦。

annotations.explanation: 可指绕开某地或绕过某个环节、限制。

examples.en: The pipeline bypasses the crowded shipping lane.
examples.zh: 这条管道绕开了拥挤的航运通道。

annotations.explanation: bring something past a level 表示使某物超过某一水平或关口。

examples.en: Strong demand could bring the price past $100.
examples.zh: 强劲需求可能使价格突破100美元。

annotations.meaningZh: 黄金的抗跌性（标题双关：bullion 黄金 + resistance 抗跌/抵抗）
annotations.explanation: 标题用 bullion（金条、黄金）与 resistance（抵抗、抗跌）组合，指黄金在压力下仍具韧性。

examples.en: Bullion resistance surprised traders this month.
examples.zh: 本月黄金的抗跌性令交易员意外。

annotations.explanation: resilience 指抗压、恢复力；remarkable 表示显著、非凡。

examples.en: The economy is showing remarkable resilience.
examples.zh: 经济正表现出显著韧性。

annotations.explanation: 此处 run 不是“跑”，而是名词“一段时期、连续表现”，如 a run of losses。

examples.en: The stock is enjoying its best run in years.
examples.zh: 该股正经历多年来最好的一段走势。

annotations.meaningZh: 一系列交织的因素；多重因素组合
annotations.explanation: cocktail 本义“鸡尾酒”，比喻多种因素混合在一起。

examples.en: A cocktail of factors pushed inflation higher.
examples.zh: 多重因素交织推高了通胀。

annotations.meaningZh: 对黄金构成压力；拖累金价
annotations.explanation: weigh on 表示对某物形成压力、拖累；it 指黄金。

examples.en: Rising yields are weighing on gold.
examples.zh: 收益率上升正拖累黄金。

annotations.explanation: rate hike 指加息；return to 表示重新回到某种政策路径。

examples.en: Markets fear a return to rate hikes.
examples.zh: 市场担心重回加息。

target.text: driven the dollar to multi-month highs

annotations.explanation: drive 表示推动、驱使；multi-month highs 指数月以来最高水平。

examples.en: Safe-haven demand drove the dollar to multi-month highs.
examples.zh: 避险需求将美元推至数月高位。

annotations.explanation: heightened 表示被推高的、加剧的；inflation expectations 是经济学术语“通胀预期”。

examples.en: The survey pointed to heightened inflation expectations.
examples.zh: 调查显示通胀预期加剧。

annotations.explanation: real yields 指扣除通胀后的实际收益率，是影响黄金的重要变量。

examples.en: Real 10-year yields have risen sharply.
examples.zh: 实际十年期收益率大幅上升。

annotations.explanation: inverse 表示相反的；inverse relationship 指一个上升时另一个下降。

examples.en: Bond prices have an inverse relationship with yields.
examples.zh: 债券价格与收益率呈反向关系。

annotations.explanation: 指资产不产生利息或股息，因此持有黄金没有收益流。

examples.en: Gold pays no income, so rates matter a lot.
examples.zh: 黄金不支付收益，因此利率很重要。

annotations.explanation: full 强调整整、足足；percentage point 是“百分点”，不是百分比变化。

examples.en: The rate rose by a full percentage point.
examples.zh: 利率上升了整整一个百分点。

target.text: Real 10-year yields, long regarded as having a key inverse relationship with the gold price as it pays no income, have risen a full percentage point this year to 2.88%.

annotations.translationZh: 长期被视为与金价存在关键反向关系的实际十年期收益率，今年已整整上升一个百分点，达到2.88%，因为黄金不支付收益。
annotations.explanation: 主语 Real 10-year yields 后接过去分词短语 long regarded as ... 作后置定语/插入说明；as it pays no income 是原因状语从句，it 指黄金。谓语 have risen 与主语相隔较远，阅读时要抓住主干。

structure.text: long regarded as having a key inverse relationship with the gold price
structure.role: 过去分词短语作后置定语/插入语
structure.note: 说明该收益率长期被视为与金价反向相关
it 指黄金，解释为何存在反向关系

examples.en: Bond yields, long watched by equity investors, have risen sharply this year.
examples.zh: 长期受股市投资者关注的债券收益率今年大幅上升。

annotations.explanation: hedge against 表示对冲、防范某种风险；debasement 指货币贬值、购买力下降。

examples.en: Investors buy gold to hedge against inflation.
examples.zh: 投资者买黄金以对冲通胀。

annotations.explanation: 原指降低硬币贵金属成色，现代常指货币购买力被稀释、贬值。

examples.en: Gold is often seen as a hedge against currency debasement.
examples.zh: 黄金常被视为对冲货币贬值的手段。

annotations.explanation: feckless 表示不负责任、无能的；fecklessly loose 指“不负责任地宽松”。

examples.en: Critics called the policy fecklessly loose.
examples.zh: 批评者称该政策是不负责任的宽松。

target.text: drove its rally to record highs

annotations.meaningZh: 推动其涨势创下历史新高
annotations.lemma: drive a rally to record highs
annotations.explanation: rally 指价格上涨、涨势；drive ... to record highs 表示推动至历史高位。

examples.en: Rate-cut hopes drove the rally to record highs.
examples.zh: 降息希望推动涨势创下历史新高。

annotations.explanation: hawkish 指倾向收紧货币政策、对抗通胀；than expected 表示比预期更甚。

examples.en: The central bank sounded more hawkish than expected.
examples.zh: 央行听起来比预期更鹰派。

annotations.meaningZh: 鹰派的（倾向收紧货币政策）
annotations.explanation: 央行语境中，hawkish 表示更关注通胀、倾向加息；反义为 dovish。

examples.en: A hawkish Fed tends to support the dollar.
examples.zh: 鹰派的美联储通常支持美元。

annotations.explanation: as of 用于表示截至某一时间点，常见于金融数据。

examples.en: As of last Friday, the fund was up 8%.
examples.zh: 截至上周五，该基金上涨了8%。

annotations.explanation: 用于排名比较，表示只排在某个对象之后。

examples.en: This was the worst month since 2020, behind only March.
examples.zh: 这是自2020年以来最糟糕的月份，仅次于3月。

annotations.meaningZh: 又一个以……为特征的年份
annotations.explanation: be marked by 表示以某事物为显著特征。

examples.en: It was a year marked by volatility.
examples.zh: 这是以波动为特征的一年。

annotations.explanation: but for 引出虚拟条件，相当于 if it were not for / if it had not been for。

examples.en: But for your help, I would have failed.
examples.zh: 要不是你的帮助，我就失败了。

annotations.meaningZh: 为金价提供底部支撑；托底
annotations.explanation: floor 在此指价格底部；put a floor under 表示防止价格进一步下跌。

examples.en: Central bank buying has put a floor under gold.
examples.zh: 央行买盘为金价提供了底部支撑。

target.text: This slide could have been a lot worse but for structural demand largely driven by central banks, which has somewhat put a floor under gold:

annotations.translationZh: 若不是主要受央行驱动的结构性需求在一定程度上为金价托底，这轮下滑本可能严重得多。
annotations.explanation: could have been 是虚拟语气，表示与事实相反的推测；but for 引出条件“要不是”。which 引导非限制性定语从句，修饰 structural demand。

structure.role: 过去分词短语作后置定语

structure.text: which has somewhat put a floor under gold
structure.note: 修饰 structural demand，说明其托底作用

examples.en: The decline could have been worse but for strong exports.
examples.zh: 要不是出口强劲，下滑本可能更糟。

annotations.explanation: 指央行等货币当局增加外汇或黄金储备。

examples.en: Reserve accumulation slowed last year.
examples.zh: 去年储备积累放缓。

annotations.explanation: appeal to 表示对某人有吸引力；monetary authorities 指央行等货币当局。

examples.en: Gold still appeals to long-term investors.
examples.zh: 黄金仍对长期投资者有吸引力。

annotations.meaningZh: 以中国为首；由中国主导
annotations.explanation: led by 表示由某人或某方带头、主导。

examples.en: The recovery was led by tech stocks.
examples.zh: 反弹由科技股主导。

annotations.explanation: 指某事物能否持续存在或保持影响力。

examples.en: Analysts question the rally’s staying power.
examples.zh: 分析人士质疑这轮涨势的持续性。

annotations.explanation: holdings 指持有的资产；increase holdings 是金融报道中“增持”的常见表达。

examples.en: Funds plan to increase their holdings of gold.
examples.zh: 基金计划增持黄金。

annotations.explanation: lean on 本义“靠在……上”，引申为依赖、倚重。

examples.en: The strategy leans on strong domestic demand.
examples.zh: 该战略倚重强劲的国内需求。

annotations.explanation: hedge 作动词表示对冲、防范；geopolitical risks 指地缘政治风险。

examples.en: Investors use gold to hedge geopolitical risks.
examples.zh: 投资者用黄金对冲地缘政治风险。

annotations.explanation: store of value 是资产功能术语，指能保存价值的资产，如黄金。

examples.en: Gold is traditionally viewed as a store of value.
examples.zh: 黄金传统上被视为价值储存手段。

annotations.explanation: constraint 表示限制、约束；constraints on 后接受限制的对象。

examples.en: There are tight constraints on new supply.
examples.zh: 新供应面临严格限制。

target.text: kept supply from keeping pace with demand

annotations.explanation: keep pace with 表示跟上、同步；keep someone/something from doing 表示阻止其做某事。

examples.en: Production has failed to keep pace with demand.
examples.zh: 生产未能跟上需求。

annotations.explanation: 表示与去年同期相比，经济数据中常用。

examples.en: Sales rose 5% year-on-year.
examples.zh: 销售额同比增长5%。

annotations.explanation: point out 表示指出、提醒某个事实或观点。

examples.en: She points out that the data is incomplete.
examples.zh: 她指出数据并不完整。

annotations.explanation: 矿业语境中 permitting 指项目获得各类许可证的审批过程，不是“允许”的现在分词。

examples.en: Mine permitting can take many years.
examples.zh: 矿山许可审批可能需要多年。

annotations.meaningZh: 成熟运营项目；成熟矿山
annotations.explanation: operations 在矿业可指运营项目、矿山；mature 表示已开发多年、进入成熟期。

examples.en: Mature operations often face higher costs.
examples.zh: 成熟矿山往往面临更高成本。

annotations.explanation: 矿业术语，grade 指矿石品位，grade decline 指矿石中有用成分含量下降。

examples.en: Grade decline is a challenge for old mines.
examples.zh: 品位下降是老矿面临的挑战。

annotations.explanation: 指项目或企业所需投入的资本规模。

examples.en: The project has huge capital requirements.
examples.zh: 该项目资本需求巨大。

annotations.explanation: bullish 表示看涨的、乐观的；用于引出支持价格上涨的理由。

examples.en: The bullish argument is that demand will remain strong.
examples.zh: 看涨的论据是需求将保持强劲。

annotations.explanation: 金融语境中指市场重新评估某资产，通常意味着估值上调。

examples.en: Analysts expect the sector to re-rate this year.
examples.zh: 分析师预计该板块今年将获重新估值。

annotations.explanation: well 用于加强 before，表示“远在……之前”。

examples.en: Prices may rise well before supply arrives.
examples.zh: 价格可能在供应到来之前很久就上涨。

annotations.meaningZh: 使有意义的新产能投产上线
annotations.explanation: bring something online 表示使设施、产能开始运营；meaningful 强调有实质意义、规模可观。

examples.en: The company will bring new capacity online next year.
examples.zh: 该公司明年将使新产能投产。

annotations.lemma: continuous flow of money into something
annotations.explanation: flow of money into 指资金流入某资产或市场；continuous 强调持续性。

examples.en: The continuous flow of money into tech funds lifted valuations.
examples.zh: 资金持续流入科技基金推高了估值。

annotations.meaningZh: 黄金支持的交易所交易基金（黄金ETF）
annotations.explanation: ETF 是以黄金为支撑、可在交易所买卖的基金，投资者无需直接持有实物黄金。

examples.en: Gold-backed exchange-traded funds saw strong demand.
examples.zh: 黄金ETF需求强劲。

annotations.explanation: 指流入资金减去流出资金后的净额，金融数据中常用。

examples.en: The fund reported net inflows of $2 billion.
examples.zh: 该基金报告净流入20亿美元。

target.text: surged more than in any month since

annotations.meaningZh: 激增幅度超过自……以来任何月份
annotations.lemma: surge more than in any month since...
annotations.explanation: surge 表示激增；more than in any month since 用于比较，强调创下某段时间以来最高。

examples.en: Inflows surged more than in any month since 2021.
examples.zh: 流入量激增，超过自2021年以来任何月份。

annotations.explanation: shrug off 字面是“耸肩摆脱”，常表示对不利因素不屑一顾或成功摆脱。这里说金价摆脱了结构性逆风。

examples.en: Investors shrugged off the weak jobs report.
examples.zh: 投资者对疲软的就业报告不以为意。

annotations.meaningZh: 结构性逆风、结构性不利因素
annotations.explanation: headwind 原指逆风，商业新闻中喻指阻碍增长或价格上涨的因素；structural 强调长期、结构性的。

examples.en: The industry faces structural headwinds from aging demographics.
examples.zh: 该行业面临人口老龄化带来的结构性逆风。

annotations.explanation: recoup 意为“收回、弥补”，常与 losses 搭配，表示挽回落差或亏损。

examples.en: The fund recouped most of its losses by year-end.
examples.zh: 该基金到年底收复了大部分失地。

annotations.explanation: hold 这里不是“握住”，而是“保持、持续”。Whether the rebound holds 指反弹能否维持。

examples.en: If the trend holds, sales will rise again next quarter.
examples.zh: 如果这一趋势保持下去，下季度销售将再次上升。

annotations.explanation: 常用插入语，表示“部分原因在于”。比 partly 更正式。

examples.en: The delay was due in part to bad weather.
examples.zh: 延误部分是因为天气恶劣。

annotations.explanation: due 后接时间，新闻中常表示数据、报告等“预计在某个时间发布”。

examples.en: The central bank decision is due Thursday.
examples.zh: 央行决定预计周四公布。

annotations.explanation: record 作形容词，表示“创纪录的、空前的”，不是名词“记录”。

examples.en: Record temperatures were recorded across Europe.
examples.zh: 欧洲各地录得创纪录气温。

annotations.explanation: keep + 宾语 + elevated 表示“使……保持高位”；reading 指数据读数。

examples.en: Supply shortages could keep inflation elevated.
examples.zh: 供应短缺可能使通胀居高不下。

annotations.explanation: reading 在统计学和新闻中常指仪器或指标显示的“读数、数据”。

examples.en: The latest reading suggests the economy is slowing.
examples.zh: 最新数据表明经济正在放缓。

annotations.explanation: headline inflation/rate 指包含所有项目的“总体”通胀率，与 core 核心通胀率相对。

examples.en: Headline inflation rose to 4%, while core inflation stayed at 2.8%.
examples.zh: 总体通胀升至4%，而核心通胀维持在2.8%。

annotations.meaningZh: 核心的（剔除食品和能源等波动项）
annotations.explanation: 核心 CPI 等指标剔除价格波动大的项目，更能反映潜在通胀趋势。

examples.en: Core prices rose more than economists expected.
examples.zh: 核心价格涨幅超过经济学家预期。

annotations.explanation: CPI 是 Consumer Price Index 的缩写，衡量一篮子消费品和服务的价格变化。

examples.en: CPI is released monthly by the statistics agency.
examples.zh: CPI由统计机构每月发布。

annotations.explanation: tick 表示价格或数据“小幅变动”，upward 指向上；tick upward 即小幅上行。

examples.en: Unemployment ticked upward to 4.1%.
examples.zh: 失业率小幅上升至4.1%。

annotations.explanation: pressure on 后接承受压力的人或资产；类似表达有 put pressure on。

examples.en: Rising yields increase the pressure on gold prices.
examples.zh: 收益率上升增加了金价承受的压力。

annotations.explanation: prospect 指“前景、可能性”，raise the prospect of 表示使某事更可能发生。

examples.en: The deal raised the prospect of a trade war.
examples.zh: 该协议提高了贸易战的可能性。

annotations.meaningZh: 在更长时间内维持高位
annotations.explanation: 固定表达 higher for longer，指利率等在经济中“更高更久”，是近年央行政策讨论常用语。

examples.en: Markets are adjusting to rates staying higher for longer.
examples.zh: 市场正在适应利率在更长时间内维持高位。

annotations.explanation: 用于引出与上文相反或抵消性的因素，相当于 on the other hand。

examples.en: Against that, lower oil prices could ease inflation.
examples.zh: 与此相对，油价下跌可能缓解通胀。

annotations.explanation: work out 在此不是“锻炼”或“解决”，而是“进展顺利、奏效”。

examples.en: If the plan works out, costs will fall sharply.
examples.zh: 如果计划奏效，成本将大幅下降。

annotations.meaningZh: 不那么受……困扰、不太在意
annotations.explanation: bothered by 表示“被……困扰”；less 表示程度减轻。

examples.en: Investors seem less bothered by the weak data.
examples.zh: 投资者似乎不太在意疲软的数据。

annotations.meaningZh: 向后看的、反映过去的、回顾性的

examples.zh: 除了这一直接因素，长期风险仍然存在。

examples.zh: 财报可能是该股的下一个催化剂。

annotations.meaningZh: 仍然牢牢起作用、仍在影响局势

examples.zh: 黄金常被视为对冲美元贬值的手段。

annotations.explanation: 指各国减少在国际贸易和储备中对美元依赖的趋势。

examples.zh: 去美元化可能重塑全球储备持有格局。

examples.en: The stock entered a powerful bull run.
examples.zh: 该股进入强劲牛市行情。

annotations.explanation: hold an outlook 表示“持有某种看法/展望”；favorable 指有利的、乐观的。

examples.en: Many analysts hold a favorable outlook for gold.
examples.zh: 许多分析师对黄金持乐观展望。

target.text: That would allow gold to decouple from real interest rates and embark on a new bull run into 2027.

annotations.translationZh: 这将使黄金得以与实际利率脱钩，并开启一轮延续到2027年的新牛市。
annotations.explanation: allow sb/sth to do 后接两个并列不定式：decouple from... 和 embark on...。

examples.en: Lower inflation would allow the economy to recover and create more jobs.
examples.zh: 通胀下降将使经济得以复苏并创造更多就业。

annotations.explanation: spike 指数据或价格的急剧上升；yields 指债券收益率。

examples.en: The spike in yields caught investors off guard.
examples.zh: 收益率飙升令投资者措手不及。

annotations.explanation: 金融语境中 yield 常指债券等投资的收益率。

examples.en: Bond yields rose after the inflation report.
examples.zh: 通胀报告后债券收益率上升。

annotations.explanation: 引导同时发生的对比情况，常译为“尽管、就在……之时”。

examples.en: Demand rose even as prices increased.
examples.zh: 尽管价格上涨，需求仍上升。

annotations.explanation: 这里不是“包含”，而指价格或局势“受控、相对稳定”。

examples.en: Price pressures remained contained.
examples.zh: 价格压力仍受控制。

examples.en: The reaction underscores the extent of investor concern.
examples.zh: 这一反应凸显了投资者担忧的程度。

examples.en: Gold's resistance surprised traders.
examples.zh: 黄金的抗跌性令交易员意外。

annotations.translationZh: 就在金价相对受控之际，收益率却大幅飙升，这凸显了黄金的抗跌程度。
annotations.explanation: 主语是 The big spike in yields，even as 引导让步/对比状语从句，谓语 underscores。

structure.text: even as gold’s price remains relatively contained

examples.zh: 成本上升之际销售却下滑，凸显了问题的严重程度。

annotations.lemma: it is premature to do something
annotations.explanation: premature 表示“过早的”，it 是形式主语，不定式是真正主语。

examples.en: It's premature to suggest the crisis is over.
examples.zh: 现在说危机结束还为时过早。

annotations.explanation: 指情况发生变化后形成的新的常规状态。

examples.en: Higher rates may become the new norm.
examples.zh: 更高的利率可能成为新常态。

annotations.explanation: hold up 在此表示价格或表现“保持良好、没有垮掉”。

examples.en: Gold has held up despite rising yields.
examples.zh: 尽管收益率上升，黄金仍保持坚挺。

annotations.explanation: 表示面对困难、压力或反对时。

examples.en: The market held up in the face of bad news.
examples.zh: 面对坏消息，市场仍保持坚挺。

annotations.explanation: surging 作形容词，表示“急剧上升的”。

examples.en: Surging yields pressured technology stocks.
examples.zh: 飙升的收益率压低了科技股。

target.text: While it’s premature to suggest a new norm, it’s striking how gold prices have held up in the face of surging yields:

annotations.translationZh: 尽管现在说出现了新常态还为时过早，但面对飙升的收益率，金价竟能保持如此坚挺，实在引人注目：
annotations.explanation: While 引导让步状语从句；主句中 it 是形式主语，how 从句说明令人惊讶的内容。

structure.text: While it’s premature to suggest a new norm

structure.note: 形式主语结构，表示令人惊讶。

structure.note: 真正主语，说明惊讶之处。

examples.zh: 尽管现在称趋势还为时过早，但情绪变化之快令人瞩目。

annotations.explanation: 表示一个因素影响或传导到另一领域。

examples.en: Higher metal prices feed into mining stocks.
examples.zh: 金属价格上涨会传导至矿业股。

examples.en: Gold equities rallied alongside the metal.
examples.zh: 黄金股随金价一同上涨。

annotations.explanation: project 作动词，表示根据现有信息“预计、推算”。

examples.en: Economists project slower growth next year.
examples.zh: 经济学家预计明年增长放缓。

annotations.explanation: 贵金属价格常用“金额 + an ounce”表示每盎司价格。

examples.en: Silver traded above $30 an ounce.
examples.zh: 白银交易价超过每盎司30美元。

annotations.explanation: margin 指利润率；help 在此表示有助于提升。

examples.zh: 价格上涨今年应有助于提高利润率。

examples.en: The company generated strong free cash flows.
examples.zh: 该公司产生了强劲的自由现金流。

annotations.explanation: urge caution 表示强烈建议保持谨慎；still 强调尽管如此。

examples.en: Analysts still urge caution despite the rally.
examples.zh: 尽管市场上涨，分析师仍呼吁谨慎。

examples.en: Investors are looking to avoid unnecessary risk.
examples.zh: 投资者力求避免不必要的风险。

annotations.explanation: guidance 指公司给出的业绩或成本预期；negative 表示不利的。

examples.en: The stock fell after negative cost guidance.
examples.zh: 在给出负面成本指引后，该股下跌。

examples.en: Mining stocks fell on production downgrades.
examples.zh: 产量下调导致矿业股下跌。

examples.zh: 利率上升会提高持有无收益资产的机会成本。

annotations.explanation: cease 表示停止；cease to exist 是正式表达，指国家、组织等消亡。

examples.en: The empire ceased to exist after the war.
examples.zh: 该帝国在战后不复存在。

annotations.explanation: 比喻新关系、新产品或新政策初期和谐顺利的阶段。

examples.en: The app is still in its honeymoon phase.
examples.zh: 这款应用仍处于蜜月期。

annotations.meaningZh: 在稳固基础上、有充分依据
annotations.explanation: 既可指物理上站在坚实地面，也可喻指论点、地位有可靠基础。

examples.en: The argument is on solid ground.
examples.zh: 这一论点有充分依据。

annotations.explanation: subscribe to 后接报刊、通讯、服务等，表示订阅。

examples.en: You can subscribe to the newsletter for free.
examples.zh: 你可以免费订阅该通讯。

annotations.explanation: 彭博观点的一个专栏名，这里作为专名整体理解。

examples.en: Points of Return is a Bloomberg Opinion newsletter.
examples.zh: 《Points of Return》是彭博观点的一份通讯。

annotations.explanation: access to 表示“使用/接触……的权限”；unlimited 强调不受限制。

examples.en: Subscribers get unlimited access to the archive.
examples.zh: 订阅者可无限制访问档案。

annotations.explanation: 指依赖数据分析、统计和事实核查的新闻报道。

examples.en: The outlet is known for data-based journalism.
examples.zh: 该媒体以数据驱动新闻著称。

annotations.explanation: newsletter 指通过邮件发送的资讯通讯；exclusive 表示仅向订阅者提供。

examples.en: The company offers exclusive daily newsletters.
examples.zh: 该公司提供独家每日通讯。

annotations.explanation: gain 表示获得；analysis from 后接来源。

examples.en: Readers gain expert analysis from top economists.
examples.zh: 读者可从顶尖经济学家处获得专业分析。
